title: Arkansas Guardsmen Assist in Hurricane Harvey Relief Efforts - Review
description:
Soldiers and Airmen of the Arkansas National Guard have rendered assistance to disaster stricken Texas. 

This video provides a brief snapshot as to what the Arkansas Guardsmen did during their deployment to various locations throughout southeast Texas.

(U.S. Army National Guard video by Spc. Stephen Wright)

transcript.text: - [Narrator] Hurricane Harvey initially made landfall
as a Category 4 hurricane
and brought with it sustained wind speeds
of over 130 miles an hour.
At the height of the storm,
the hurricane dropped roughly 52 inches of rain
over a vast majority of Southeast Texas.
The water and wind from the monstrous
hurricane devastated portions of Texas,
which warranted the Texas governor assembling and activating
the entire Texas Military Department.
One trillion gallons of water was reportedly dumped
on Harris County alone in four days.
On August 27th, Arkansas's governor, Asa Hutchinson,
ordered the 61st Civil Support Team
to deploy to Texas in order to assist
in disaster relief operations,
specifically hazmat response efforts.
Just five days later,
Hutchinson spoke with A.J. Gary,
the Director of the Arkansas Department
of Emergency Management,
and Major General Mark H. Berry,
The Adjutant General of the Arkansas National Guard,
and made the determination that Arkansas
would deploy over 1,000 more guardsmen
to Texas to support ongoing relief and recovery
operations at the request of the State of Texas.
The Arkansas National Guard met the needs
of the State of Texas by deploying
in total nearly 1,300 soldiers and Airmen.
The guardsmen brought with them over 400 vehicles,
including C-130s and UH-60 Black Hawks.
Every major command of the Arkansas National Guard
was involved with relief efforts in some form.
All personnel and equipment were utilized
to augment the Texas National Guard
as a combined and joint effort
of numerous government agencies,
ranging from local volunteers,
Texas State agencies, to the FBI.
Arkansas was able to assist in an extremely wide variety
of operations by providing support in areas
such as communications assistance,
military aircraft transportation,
high-water rescue and recovery operations,
air traffic control support,
food service and distribution,
damage assessment teams, security operations,
vehicle and equipment maintenance,
air and water chemical assessments,
intelligence, weather surface support,
and joint operations center staffing.
Just to name a few, Arkansas guardsmen
distributed much-needed items,
such as food, water, and blankets.
Along with high-water rescues,
guardsmen assisted in the rescue
of stranded animals near Angleton, Texas.
Arkansas not only provided ground support
for operations, they also brought with them
a Mobile Emergency Operations Center,
also known as a MEOC, to serve
as a joint task force command unit.
Arkansas's response to Hurricane Harvey
is the second largest domestic response
that the Arkansas National Guard has undertaken.
The Harvey response is second only
to the Hurricane Katrina response in 2005.
The role of the Arkansas National Guard
has now shifted from Hurricane Harvey relief operations
to Hurricane Irma relief operations.
In North Little Rock for the Arkansas National Guard,
I'm Specialist Stephen Wright. (gentle music)
